depth: The monocular depth map presents a top-down salon view, with the seated person's foil-covered head positioned directly in front of and beneath the standing camera wearer at roughly 0.4–0.6 metres, forming the brightest foreground region. To the right, within arm's reach at 0.6–0.9 metres, is a tray table carrying a dye bowl, foil, and a towel, along with an empty salon chair at 1.0–1.3 metres. Past the seated client, the wall mirrors and drawer cabinets lie about 1.5–2.5 metres away; frame 3 also shows a second worker crouched on the left around 1.2–1.5 metres away near the client's extended foot and blue foot-bath basin. The client and workers face away from or downward relative to the camera wearer instead of looking upward. In frames 4 and 5, the camera wearer's black-gloved left arm enters at 0.2–0.4 metres as pure white, partially covering the client's head and lying about 0.4 metres left of the right-hand dye bowl. Relative to RGB alone, the depth map distinctly divides the foreground head, mid-ground tray and chair armrests, and receding wall cabinets into separate distance layers despite the complicated visual clutter. It is unreliable around the wall mirrors, however, because virtual reflections of the salon chair, foot basin, and opposite room receive false recessed depths of 2.5–3.5 metres rather than the mirror glass's flat plane at ~1.6 metres.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map captures very little of the salon arrangement: objects appear only in frames 1, 3, and 4, while frames 2 and 5 and every background mirror, cabinet, tray, and chair remain entirely unsegmented. In frame 1, the model finds the seated client's head in the lower-left foreground at ~0.5 metres from the camera wearer and within arm's reach, but incorrectly calls the foil-covered hair a 'couch'. It labels only a tiny portion of the client's lower-left leg or foot, around 1.2 metres away, as 'person'. When the camera shifts slightly left in frame 3, the second worker crouching in the upper-left at ~1.3 metres, facing the client's extended foot within that worker's arm's reach and ~0.8 metres from the client's torso, is wrongly classified as a 'dog'; the client and foreground tools are missed altogether. Frame 4 correctly isolates the joined outline of the camera wearer's reaching left arm at 0.2–0.4 metres and the client's obscured head at 0.5 metres as one 'person' mask, although it merges two people and overlooks the wearer's right hand beside the dye bowl. The frame-4 boundary cleanly separates this foreground human silhouette from the dark floor and chair background, but the map remains highly unreliable because of severe top-down perspective distortion, substantial occlusion from hair foils and capes, and incorrect or merged category labels.
pose: Across the five-frame sequence, the body-and-hand skeleton map is nearly completely empty: it identifies just one yellow body skeleton in frame 3's upper-left quadrant and detects nothing in frames 1, 2, 4, or 5. That frame-3 skeleton marks the second person crouching on the floor about 1.2–1.5 metres to the camera wearer's left-front and approximately 0.8 metres in front of the seated client. The person is oriented toward the lower-right, where the client's lower legs stretch into a foot basin within the crouching person's arm's reach. The displayed head, torso, shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, and knee keypoints indicate that this person bends downward toward the client's foot while facing away from the camera wearer. In comparison with the dark clothing and difficult overhead perspective in the RGB strip, the frame-3 skeleton makes the worker's compact, bent-knee stance and reaching arm clearer. Nevertheless, pose estimation is mostly unreliable for this sharply angled egocentric view: it entirely misses the seated client immediately below the camera at 0.4–0.6 metres, obscured by hair foils and a cape; loses the crouching worker when the frame edge partially cuts them off elsewhere; and finds no magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's black-gloved hands reaching at 0.2–0.6 metres throughout frames 1 to 5.
